body:
> I wonder if this check is necessary as there is another check later that verifies that the space state is available

The check in `JoltPhysicsServer3D::space_get_direct_state` should arguably be done within each method of `JoltPhysicsDirectSpaceState3D` instead, as opposed to in `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::space_get_direct_state`, since it's pretty easy to bypass this whole thing by just caching the space state reference and misuse it later (without any error-checking) but I mostly just mimicked what Godot Physics was doing.

With that said, I must admit I also don't know why that main thread check is there. As far as I know all physics queries in Godot Physics are read-only operations, so should inherently be thread-safe so long as you're not doing anything else physics-related at the same time. It's not like the internal space state reference ever gets written to outside of the space constructor either, so there are no concerns about race conditions there.

But again, you can technically work around this by just caching the `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D` reference from somewhere "safe", and then use it from whatever thread you want. Just be careful not to perform any physics queries outside of `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces`.

> Removing the main thread check in a custom build allows my project to work with the integrated Jolt physics module just as it currently does with the GDExtension version. It seems GDExtensions bypass this main thread check.

The GDExtension didn't "bypass" it, because it isn't thread-safe (as mentioned [here](https://github.com/godot-jolt/godot-jolt?tab=readme-ov-file#whats-not-supported)) and therefore doesn't support operations from anywhere but the main thread, including physics queries (which are not read-only with how Jolt is integrated).

I should add this prevents `Raycast3D` from functioning if it is in a sub thread group.

Is this a case of Jolt would need to be made thread-safe before this could be allowed when using Jolt?

> I should add this prevents `Raycast3D` from functioning if it is in a sub thread group.

I must admit I don't know what the status is of that sub-thread grouping feature, or whether all built-in scene nodes are expected to work with it, but it does sound like this could be reason enough to remove that main thread check.

> Is this a case of Jolt would need to be made thread-safe before this could be allowed when using Jolt?

The built-in Jolt module in 4.4 should already (assuming no mistakes on my part) be thread-safe, in largely the same way as Godot Physics, although it hasn't been tested much.

So not being able to use `RayCast3D` with sub-thread groups should be applicable to both engines, and not unique to the Jolt integration.

Will this little restriction be removed in the future? I have some addons that don't work because they do these physics queries outside of physics process. I'm still not sure why this whole checking is required, one of the comments mention that these are read only operations but that's for Godot physics and not Jolt. But I assume it's the same for Jolt as well.
